plans.note: Cap in 21.1 is mutual at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000; Excluded Claims defined in 21.3 and consequential-damages carve-outs in 21.2. Check cap adequacy against Fees and confirm data/security, indemnity, IP, fraud carve-outs are complete and that unpaid Fees sit outside the cap. Note 18.2 (insurance does not limit liability) as supporting cross-reference.

Vendor IP indemnity in 20.1 and conduct/data/law indemnity in 20.2; Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is already narrowed with exclusions. Verify 20.4 procedure (defence control with indemnified party, no prejudicial settlement) and 20.5 mitigation/refund remedy, which Section 9.3 cross-references.

Section 12.3 affirmatively confirms no non-compete, exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment by Customer; confirm no conflicting restriction elsewhere (2.2 exclusivity clause conflicts and should be read together).
Section 2.2 (first instance) makes Vendor Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics — off-playbook and directly contrary to 2.1 and 12.3. Target deletion.

Section 7.2 (first instance) obliges Customer to give Vendor terms no less favourable than any other supplier — wrong-direction MFN; delete and rely on 12.3's confirmation that no MFN commitment exists.

Section 12.4 binds only Customer, runs 18 months post-termination, covers anyone employed at any time and bars engagement with no general-advertising carve-out; narrow to 12 months, personnel directly involved, solicitation only, with advertising/inbound carve-out, and make mutual.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency and security/SLA termination rights (note missing 9.4); no Customer termination for convenience appears. Propose adding Customer-only convenience termination on 30–60 days' notice with pro-rata refund, keyed to the refund mechanics in 10.2.
Section 8.2 requires 180 days' non-renewal notice — too long; reduce to 30–60 days. Section 8.3 uplift (lesser of CPI and 3%, 90 days' notice) is acceptable; confirm no increase on prepaid periods.
New York law with New York County courts and no arbitration — compliant. Confirm CISG waiver and that the 28.3 escalation does not delay urgent injunctive relief.

24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors, 24.2 restricts Vendor, and 24.4 blocks Vendor termination or repricing on our change of control — aligned. Check 24.3's residual mutual consent language does not swallow 24.1 and that 13.3 licence transfer tracks Section 24.

14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP; 14.2 assigns Deliverables to Customer subject to payment. Verify definitions in 1.3/1.4/1.8 do not carve our material into Vendor Technology, and that 15.1 processing rights (including no model training) stay limited.

13.1 covers Affiliates and contractors; 13.2 grants a perpetual paid-up licence; 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to material uncured breach after cure opportunity. Confirm 13.4 restrictions and the 14.3 cross-reference do not undercut the grant.

Section 22.1 permits Vendor audits at any time without notice with remote system access — off-playbook; require 30 days' notice, once per 12 months, business hours, off-site records review, no direct system access. 22.2/22.3 (Vendor cost unless >5% shortfall, confidentiality of findings) are acceptable; check Section 23 for overlapping records rights.

Section 7.6 imposes USD 25,000/day liquidated damages on Customer for dependency delays — delete; at most Vendor gets excused performance and an equitable timeline adjustment. Cross-check interaction with the mutual cap in 21.1.

19.1–19.3 give services, conformity, malicious-code and compliance warranties; 19.2 Deliverable period is 90 days — consider extending to 12 months. Confirm 19.4 remedy includes refund and is non-exclusive, and that 19.5's disclaimer preserves express warranties and indemnities; acceptance mechanics in 6.1/6.2 are related.

Section 18.1 covers CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M for the term plus one year; 18.2 adds certificates and confirms insurance does not cap liability. Check E&O adequacy relative to Fees and the cancellation-notice qualifier.

Section 2.1 expressly disclaims minimum quantity or purchase commitments and 12.3 confirms no minimum-volume obligation; verify 7.1's bar on minimum-use charges is preserved and that no Order Form-level commitment is imported.

Section 11 provides up to six months' transition assistance, 30-day data return in machine-readable form with no fee-dispute hold-back, and certified deletion. Confirm consistency with 10.1/10.2 wind-down and refunds and with 16.5's return/destroy obligation.
